subject: Math
subskill: Evaluate Function at a Given Value
prompt:
The function $f(x)$ is given as
$f(x) = q((x - 10)^{2} + r)((x - 10)^{2} + s)$
The graph of $y = f(x)$ passes through $(13, 18)$ and $(5, 24)$. What is the value of $f(7) + f(15)$?
explanation: Choice B is correct. The function $f(x) = q((x - 10)^2 + r)((x - 10)^2 + s)$ depends only on $(x - 10)^2$, so $f(x)$ is symmetric about $x = 10$. For $x = 13$: $(13 - 10)^2 = 9$. For $x = 7$: $(7 - 10)^2 = 9$. Since both give the same value of $(x - 10)^2$, we have $f(7) = f(13) = 18$. Similarly, for $x = 5$: $(5 - 10)^2 = 25$. For $x = 15$: $(15 - 10)^2 = 25$. So $f(15) = f(5) = 24$. Therefore, $f(7) + f(15) = 18 + 24 = 42$.
